name: Village of Sleepy Hollow
gaps: Schedule sets no maximum stories, floor area/FAR, impervious coverage, lot frontage or lot depth for residence districts.
Corner-lot street-side setback depends on the adjoining lot's front yard (§ 450-40D); corner_side_ft left null.
§ 450-40 was amended 7-28-2026 (L.L. 9-2026); text read on eCode360 2026-11-25 shows no FAR/impervious rule, but the Schedule attachment is Supp 15 (Nov 2022).
R-6 (not a county RES district) included with cross-referenced R-5 values; lot width ambiguous.
RF (Riverfront Development, Art. IV) and SRF overlay residential rules not researched; no local steep-slope chapter or accessory-apartment provision found.

wetlands.summary: Ch. 418: wetlands, watercourses and a 100 ft buffer around each (more where DEC or the approval authority designates) are regulated; regulated activities need a wetland permit.

trees.summary: Ch. 385: Tree Officer permit to remove trees 8 in. DBH or larger on private or Village property, except trees within 10 ft of a building, dead or hazardous trees, or removals shown on an approved site plan.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 358 and Ch. 450 Art. XVI: SWPPP required for land development disturbing 1 acre or more (or part of a larger common plan).

general.accessory_structures: Detached accessory structures: not in the required front yard, side/rear setback half the principal side yard (min 3 ft), 10 ft from the principal building, max 15 ft high, max 30% of the required rear yard; on corner lots principal-building rules apply (§ 450-36E).
general.pools: Building permit plus Planning Board site plan review; not within 25 ft of side/rear lot lines in R-1 or 10 ft elsewhere, not in a required front yard; 4 ft locking fence (§ 450-45).
general.notes: Fences max 3 ft in front yards and 5 ft in side/rear yards (§ 450-40F). Corner sight triangle 10 ft.

R-1.name: R-1 One-Family Residence/Open

accessory.notes: Detached accessory: not in the required front yard; side and rear setback = half the principal side yard, min 3 ft; 10 ft from the principal building; may cover max 30% of the required rear yard (§ 450-36E).

R-1.source: § 450-35 Schedule of Regulations (Attachment 1, Supp 15 Nov 2022), residence-use rows; § 450-36E
R-1.notes: Residence use: 1 acre, 150 ft width. Golf course/country club: 40 acres, 500 ft width, 5% coverage. Corner lots: street-side setback at least half the front yard required on the adjoining lot (lots existing at adoption) or the full adjoining front yard (newer subdivision lots) (§ 450-40D). New buildings may not project past the average front setback of existing buildings on the block (§ 450-40B).

R-5.notes: 1- or 2-family residence: 4,000 sf, 40 ft width; coverage 'As in R-4' (35%). Multiple dwellings: 5,000 sf for the first 3 units + 1,500 sf each additional, 50 ft width, 30% coverage; other uses 25/10/20/25 yards. Corner lots: street-side setback at least half the front yard required on the adjoining lot (lots existing at adoption) or the full adjoining front yard (newer subdivision lots) (§ 450-40D). R-6.source: § 450-35 Schedule of Regulations (Attachment 1, Supp 15 Nov 2022), residence-use rows; § 450-36E
R-6.notes: Not a county RES district; residences permitted 'As in R-5'. Lot area and coverage for 1-/2-family homes follow R-5 by cross-reference; the 100 ft width entry appears tied to multiple dwellings (width left null). Yards for all uses except multiple/attached dwellings: 20/10/20/25. Height limit 100 ft is district-wide. Corner lots: street-side setback at least half the front yard required on the adjoining lot (lots existing at adoption) or the full adjoining front yard (newer subdivision lots) (§ 450-40D). New buildings may not project past the average front setback of existing buildings on the block (§ 450-40B).
